messages:
Emma (Sales): FYI Javier's POC can't reach our private endpoint from their dev VPC. They see TLS handshake failures + DNS resolving to public IP. Can eng take a look?
Javier (Customer): repro steps: inside my EC2 I run `curl -v https://private-api.redwood.internal/health` and get `* TLS handshake timeout` then `Connection reset by peer`. DNS returns 54.12.34.56 (public).
Alice (Eng): thanks — looks like either the Private Hosted Zone isn't associated with their VPC or their resolver is hitting a public route. Javier, can you paste `dig +short private-api.redwood.internal @169.254.169.253` and `curl -v --resolve private-api.redwood.internal:443:10.2.5.12 https://private-api.redwood.internal/health` output?
Javier (Customer): `dig` returned `10.2.5.12`. curl with --resolve gives a cert error: `SSL: certificate subject name 'api.redwood.com' does not match 'private-api.redwood.internal'`. If I don't --resolve it hits 54.12.34.56.
Ben (Ops): quick checklist: 1) confirm Route53 private hosted zone associated with the right VPC(s), 2) check VPC resolver rules (forwarding to inbound resolver endpoints), 3) SG/NACL egress to our endpoint IP/port 443. Javier, can you paste your SG egress rules?
Javier (Customer): SG egress is 0.0.0.0/0:443 allowed. NACL is open.
Siva (SRE): The cert CN mismatch is expected — our hosted cert is for `api.redwood.com`. For Private deployments we issue a customer-scoped cert. Two options: 1) we can generate a cert that includes `private-api.redwood.internal` as SAN (needs CSR from you + CA approval), or 2) use SNI override as temp workaround: `curl --resolve private-api.redwood.internal:443:10.2.5.12 -H 'Host: private-api.redwood.internal' https://private-api.redwood.internal` — but if our server presents `api.redwood.com` you'll still get name mismatch unless SNI/Host match the cert.
Alice (Eng): Another quick workaround for testing: add `/etc/hosts` mapping `10.2.5.12 private-api.redwood.internal` on the client and use `curl --connect-to` to force SNI: `curl -v --connect-to private-api.redwood.internal:443:10.2.5.12 -H 'Host: api.redwood.com' https://private-api.redwood.internal/health`. This will let you confirm network path and TLS handshake separately.
Javier (Customer): tried hosts mapping + connect-to and now TLS handshake succeeds but response 403 Forbidden. Logs show `client cert required`.
Ben (Ops): ah — our private endpoint is configured behind a mutual-TLS enforcement for that environment. Did the POC request include a client cert?
Emma (Sales): they said no, we were testing basic connectivity first.
Siva (SRE): On Redwood side, we also saw a few spike rejections earlier — temporarily our edge returned 429 for a minute due to a rate-limit rule applied to unknown client IPs from private endpoints. I've disabled the strict rule for their CIDR (10.2.0.0/16) now. Javier, can you retry?
Javier (Customer): retrying... curl now: 200 OK! health: {"status":"ok","version":"r-1.4.2"}. Thanks.
Alice (Eng): good. Next steps: 1) we'll provision a customer-scoped certificate (or you can upload a cert) — Siva will coordinate. 2) Confirm VPC DHCP option set or resolver rules so the VPC uses Route53 inbound resolver when resolving `*.redwood.internal`. 3) If you keep mutual-TLS turned off for the POC, ensure auth is limited by IP allowlist.
Siva (SRE): I'll open a secure ticket to request cert CSR and put in rotation plan. Also please check OCSP stapling: we saw one client fail because their firewall stripped OCSP responses; if you have a strict TLS proxy, allow OCSP responses through.
Javier (Customer): noted. For firewall: vendor is Zscaler — will allow OCSP and SNI.
Emma (Sales): pricing question from Javier: if we need a customer cert + dedicated pool for POC, does that affect cost?
Alice (Eng): Dedicated pool adds reserved capacity cost; cert management is part of Private deployment onboarding (no extra line item for a single cert). I'll loop in Solutions Eng with rough estimate.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout for private endpoint certs in 2h — please confirm maintenance window if you want zero-downtime swap.
Ben (Ops): final note: If anyone hits `Connection reset by peer` again, grab `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.5.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/pkt.pcap` and share. That's been the fastest way to identify middlebox resets.
Emma (Sales): thanks everyone — Javier, I'll book a follow-up for cert handoff + pricing tomorrow. :thumbsup:
